items.title: Three Years of 80% Charge Limits on iPhone: The Results
items.snippet: Since 2023, Apple's newer iPhones have had an 80 percent charge limit for those who want to extend battery lifespan. Charging to 80 percent instead of 100 percent is supposed to put less stress on the battery, improving longevity. For the last three years, I've used that setting on my iPhone. I started with the iPhone 15 Pro Max , then did the iPhone 16 Pro Max , and most recently, the iPhone 17 Pro Max. After 12 months at an 80 percent maximum charge, my iPhone 17 Pro Max is at 97 percent maximum capacity with a cycle count of 277. items.title: Today in Apple history: Michael Dell says he'd shut down Apple
items.snippet: October 6, 1997: Michael Dell makes an incredibly bleak appraisal of Apple’s fortunes, uttering a quote that will become notorious. Asked what he would do with the struggling company, the founder of Dell Inc. says he would “shut it down and give the money back to the shareholders.” As incorrect forecasts go, this ultimately will go down as one of the more notable in tech history. But it doesn’t seem that way at the time. Sometimes even the tech industry’s smartest people prove spectacularly bad at seeing what comes next. In 1997, Michael Dell had plenty of reason to think Apple was finished. The company was hemorrhaging money, its product strategy was an utter mess, and Apple co-founder Steve Jobs had just returned to the company he’d been forced out of a decade and a half before. What Dell didn’t know was that Apple was standing at the edge of one of the greatest turnarounds in business history — and his throwaway remark would become a perfect reminder that even industry giants can mistake a company’s darkest moment for its final chapter. items.title: New tool removes Apple Intelligence from macOS 27 to reclaim storage
items.snippet: A new open-source tool lets Mac users remove Apple Intelligence from macOS 27 and regain 12GB of storage or more. Named RemoveMacAI, the tool runs from Terminal. Apple took away the Apple Intelligence master switch in macOS 27. Now, if you turn off individual features, the AI models still sit on your drive. On a Mac with a small SSD, that’s a lot of dead weight. Apple Intelligence takes up gigabytes of storage on a Mac because many of its AI models run locally rather than sending everything to Apple’s servers. This helps protect users’ privacy while speeding up tasks. macOS stores these models on the Mac so features such as Writing Tools, Image Playground, etc., can work without constantly uploading your data to the cloud. But, understandably, anyone not interested in macOS 27’s AI capabilities might want those gigabytes of storage back. And RemoveMacAI does the job. It’s free and is available on GitHub under the MIT license. It requires macOS 27 and a Mac with Apple silicon. You can either install it with one-line curl command or through Homebrew. items.snippet: Macworld Prime Day is here, and for the first time in months, we’re actually getting proper discounts on Apple gear. items.title: Best USB-C hubs and adapters for Mac 2026
items.snippet: Macworld USB-C and its Thunderbolt variant are the most up-to-date standards of the USB connector. They allow data-transfer speeds of up to 80Gbps, can fast-charge devices up to 240W, and conveniently fit in a port either way up—which means that you can wave bye-bye to the age-old USB guessing game of “Which way does it go in?”. USB-C is no one-trick pony—handling data transfer, video output and power input. You’ll find faster variants of USB-C (called Thunderbolt 3, 4 or 5) on Macs. Each version of Thunderbolt is backwards compatible with USB-C so the adapters reviewed here will all work with modern Macs—from the MacBooks Neo, Air and Pro, through to the desktop iMac, Mac mini and Studio. items.title: Apple will reportedly hold not one but two sets of product launches this month
items.snippet: Macworld September is the most important month in Apple’s calendar, featuring updates to the iPhone, Apple Watch, and (frequently) AirPods. But this year, October looks set to be even busier , and perhaps even more critical to the company’s long-term prospects. Hints from the rumorsphere last week strongly suggested that Apple will announce a raft of smart-home products on October 13 , likely including a HomePad smart hub and potentially including a new Apple TV and HomePod mini as well. But separate sources now indicate that this momentous unveiling won’t be the last set of Apple launches this month. items.snippet: The MALFEX campaign is an npm software supply-chain attack: malicious packages can expose developers and systems that install them to malware. Three packages were still installable as of October 1, including function-flag, which accounts for 37,419 of the campaign’s 40,767 downloads. Researchers have identified eight malicious packages linked to the operation, active since 2023, that deliver the Overlord remote-access trojan, an information stealer, or a downloader. Function-flag presents itself as an ASCII-art utility, but its postinstall script can download a payload. Source

This is a feature available in Juniper switches that can segment LAN traffic using group policy tags without the complexity associated with VXLAN or other segmentation mechanisms. items.title: HW090: Inside eduroam
items.snippet: Keith Parsons talks with Mary Bull from Internet2 to discuss the history and widespread deployment of eduroam, a global Wi-Fi roaming service supporting research and education networks. Together they discuss the technical scale of the US eduroam infrastructure, recent load-balancing improvements, and strategies for modernizing campus Wi-Fi.
